subject: Renewal health: usage signal playbook & risk triage
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@skylineai.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@skylineai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal health: usage signal playbook & risk triage

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I pulled together a short usage snapshot and an initial playbook that outlines options for the upcoming renewal based on the last six months of traffic. Quick highlights up front:

- Token run rate: ~12.4M tokens/month average, with a recent two-week spike to ~28M tokens driven by a new batch ingestion pipeline.
- Cost mix: 68% generation (chat), 22% embeddings (indexing), 10% reranking.
- Perf: p95 latency target is 220ms; current p95 across your primary model is 250–290ms under peak bursts.

Attached: usage_report_Q1_2028.pdf — contains the token breakdown by route, latency histograms, and a short root-cause hypothesis for the spike.

Given the variability, we see three practical paths that balance economics and uptime:
1) Staged uplift (recommended): +30% committed capacity for 12 months, with a mid-term review at month 4 and automated burst credits for peak days.
2) Conservative extension: keep current commit but add a burst pool and expanded cache configuration — lower unit discount, higher overage risk.
3) Ramp & true-up: monthly ramp schedule tied to traffic thresholds; true-up invoice at quarter end.

Can you confirm who from your side will own procurement + engineering sign-off? We can draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) for option 1 and include a proposed $15k one-time migration/adoption credit to offset the short-term cost of the new pipeline.

If helpful, I can run a micro-benchmark next week (15–30 min) with our ops team to validate p95 under the proposed batch window.

Best,
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Cc: procurement@skylineai.com
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health: usage signal playbook & risk triage

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the write-up and the report. A couple quick clarifying questions before we loop procurement in: 

- Can you break down which routes caused the 2x–2.5x spike? Our infra team wants to know if this was an embeddings repopulate job or chat traffic.
- If we take the +30% committed path, what is the estimated monthly spend delta vs current bill (ballpark)?
- For the $15k credit, is that refundable or applied against first-month charges?

Also, we've had some concern about SLA credits for the past quarter — could you point me to where you tracked the p95 miss and whether that qualifies for a credit under our current contract?

On procurement: procurement@skylineai.com is on the thread. Tom (cc) will coordinate with engineering and procurement.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Park
Head of Product Intelligence, Skyline AI
lydia.park@skylineai.com | +1 (617) 555-0789

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal health: usage signal playbook & risk triage (internal)

Monica / Jordan —

Spun up a quick options grid after reviewing the usage report. My recommendation is to present a clear economic trade-off with an immediate mitigation to reduce latency risk during the spike window. Draft below:

Option A — Staged uplift (Recommended)
- Commit: +30% for 12 months (applies across chat & embeddings)
- Commercial: 8% blended discount vs current effective rate
- One-time: $15k adoption credit applied to invoice month 1
- Ops: enable LRU prefix caching + 2x batch-concurrency for nightly ingestion windows
- Risk: upfront cost increase; fixes p95 during spikes in our tests

Option B — Conservative extension
- Commit: no change to base commit
- Add: Dedicated burst pool (pay-per-use) + ops changes
- Commercial: 3% rebate on overages over threshold
- Risk: higher unit cost under sustained growth

Option C — Ramp & True-up
- Commit schedule: +10% month 1, +20% month 3, +30% month 6; quarterly true-up
- Commercial: standard commit discount tiers; true-up invoice at quarter close
- Risk: administrative complexity; avoids large upfront spend

Other notes:
- Recommend we pre-author a one-time SLA goodwill credit for the quarter if customer confirms option A within 10 business days (we can structure as a billing credit).
- Jordan: ops estimate on implementing caching + batch-concurrency change? Can you provide a short ops time estimate (days) and whether this requires any config change on their side?

If we present Option A with the adoption credit and an explicit MAP timeline (30/60/90 days milestones), I think we keep renewal momentum and reduce churn risk.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health: usage signal playbook & risk triage

Hi Lydia / Tom / procurement —

Thanks for the quick review and for looping procurement in. Based on your ask and internal alignment, here's a pragmatic MAP we can execute this week to lock in capacity and reduce operational risk: 

1) Agree to Option A (Staged uplift): +30% committed capacity for 12 months.
2) Financials: we will apply the $15k one-time adoption credit against your first invoice after amendment effective date. We will also offer a conditional SLA goodwill credit up to $7,500 if p95 > 300ms for two consecutive business days during the first 60 days post-change.
3) Ops work: Jordan's team will enable LRU prefix caching and increase batch concurrency for your nightly ingestion window. Jordan: target ETA 5 business days once we have a migration window.
4) Procurement: Monica to send the MAP + simple amendment (term change + capacity table). Procurement to confirm PO path and whether DocuSign is acceptable for signature.

Next steps — proposed schedule:
- Monday (05/15) 11:00am PT: 30-min ops sync (Jordan + Tom + our ops engineer)
- Tuesday (05/16) EOD: redwood to send MAP + amendment draft
- Friday (05/19): target sign-off if procurement signs PoS / DocuSign

DocuSign link (prepped): https://www.docusign.com/tx/ABCD1234-skyline-renewal
MAP attachment: MAP_skyline_renewal_2028.docx (DOCX, 48KB)

Lydia — if that timeline looks good, I'll queue the amendment and calendar invites.

Best,
Monica
